pages.title: It Grows Itself
pages.text: I never laid a second stone. I gave the altar what its next tier asked for, and it opened a rift over itself and grew. Pillars rose out of the floor, the platform climbed, the core rose with it.$(br2)Three tiers. The higher it stood, the more it could make.

pages.title: Loud Work
pages.text: Growth is loud. Near a sculk shrieker it shrieks, and something in the city answers. Anywhere else it draws monsters out of the dark.$(br2)Twelve blocks of wool or carpet within five of the core muffle it. I learned that the hard way. Twice.

pages.title: In the Way
pages.text: The rift eats loose ground, stone and sculk in its path. Anything else stops it, and the altar told me which block and where. Once I cleared it, it went on.$(br2)When a pillar was broken, the altar kept the tier it had earned. I laid the first stones again and the rift grew back the rest. Even carried away, the core remembers.

pages.title: Every Structure
pages.text: Everything I built down here works this way. I set the first tier by hand. It forms. The rift grows every tier after it from what I give.$(br2)That is the one law of this book. I will not write it again.
